state.question: In which video is there an unnecessary action that should not have been performed during assembly?
state.summary: Current evidence is projected. Video 2 shows a body/chassis assembly followed by chassis manipulation and interior-component adjustment, which is the most consistent with an unnecessary detach/rework during assembly. Video 1 and Video 3 evidence mainly supports attachment actions and does not provide a stronger comparable candidate. R01/R02 remain partially ambiguous, but additional local probes are not expected to overturn the best-supported choice.

review.reason: Evidence from indices 15-17 confirms continued chassis manipulation but fails to resolve whether the specific action was a reversal of a previous separation or a standard assembly step due to ambiguity in the visual sequence.

inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision; Reasoner ALIGN may then rebuild the evidence synthesis when useful. Completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If residual uncertainty remains when answering, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.
